dedupe_keys.name: imax office bioretention swales mississauga soil moisture monitoring of infiltration performance step and credit valley conservation

description: This monitoring study checks whether two bioretention swales in the parking lot of the IMAX corporate office in Mississauga, Ontario, perform as designed, using soil moisture and soil temperature probes that keep working in winter. The Sustainable Technologies Evaluation Program of the Toronto and Region Conservation Authority reports it, building on a 2022 Credit Valley Conservation performance assessment of the site. Coverage is one 1.0 ha drainage area in the Sheridan Creek subwatershed, monitored for about a year and a half with shallow and deep probes upstream and downstream in each swale. Soil moisture rose quickly after rain and fell back close to the 24-hour drawdown design, and although frozen soil made winter patterns irregular, behaviour recovered soon after thaw. Format and access: a free web report; data are shown as figures. Licence: TRCA website terms; free to read. Caveats: one site, and soil moisture is an indirect measure of infiltration. It gives evidence for operating and maintaining green stormwater infrastructure in cold climates. Related catalogue records are the NGIF sensor data and the SuDS Manual.

outcomes: Soil moisture rose rapidly after rain and fell back close to the 24-hour drawdown design, so the swales nearly meet design criteria; frozen soils made patterns irregular in winter, but behaviour recovered quickly after thaw, so soil moisture probes can track performance year-round.
